item.title: Clashes at Besiktas match against Israeli club spark diplomatic row
item.description:
Istanbul club Besiktas' supporters unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during a UEFA Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia on Thursday, prompting a police response and sparking a diplomatic incident that led Turkey's foreign minister to contact his Georgian counterpart.

Turkish football fans clashed with police in Batumi, temporarily halting the match, which had been moved from Istanbul over security concerns.

item.title: Turkish elections to be held in 2028, ruling alliance agrees on Erdogan candidacy, vice president says
item.description:
ANKARA, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Turkey's elections will be held in 2028 and may be brought forward somewhat from the scheduled time in May, Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said on Thursday, adding the ruling alliance agreed that PresidentTayyip Erdogan would run again.

"The election will be held in 2028. There is a discussion about whether it could be held one month earlier or two months earlier. It could be brought forward somewhat."

"There is already a consensus within the alliance for Erdogan to run again as a candidate."

item.title: Russell plays it straight in Verstappen feud, focuses on racing
item.description:
George Russell on Thursday responded to Max Verstappen's taunting putdowns of his talent and potential, congratulating him on his Las Vegas win and conceding that that he was amused by the Dutchman's comments, but not cowed.

The Mercedes driver, who finished ninth behind Red Bull's Verstappen after hitting the barriers in the closing laps of last Sunday's Las Vegas Grand Prix, told reporters that he was putting their latest feud behind him.

item.title: Egyptians mourn, demand accountability after deadly tanker explosion kills 31
item.description:
CAIRO, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Egyptian lawmakers demanded accountability on Thursday as shocked Cairo residents mourned the deaths of 31 people in an overnight tanker explosion, the deadliest of a series of recent accidents that have stoked public anger.

The accident was caused when a car hit the back of the tanker, causing it to overturn and catch fire, public prosecutors said, adding that a suspect has been arrested.

item.title: Settlers smash foundations of Palestinian family's homes in West Bank
item.description:
By Pesha Magid

JALOUD, West Bank, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Militant Israeli settlers smashed the foundations of two homes belonging to a Palestinian family in the West Bank on Thursday, after settler attacks prevented the family from returning to them in defiance of an Israeli court order.

Security cameras showed the settlers bringing a bulldozer to the hilltop two-storey houses on either side of a road in the village of Jaloud at around 1 a.m. and spending about an hour damaging the houses. The family said it had been forced out months ago.

item.title: Pro-monarchist Iran activists disrupt Paris event: videos
item.description:
Activists backing Iran's ousted monarchy disrupted an event in Paris aiming to amplify the voices of Iranian women, prompting a bitter dispute Thursday between supporters of the deposed shah and left-wing opponents of the Islamic republic.

Analysts said the incident late Wednesday at the Arab World Institute (IMA) highlighted the entrenched divisions between diaspora opponents of the clerical leadership in Tehran, even after a wave of protests earlier this year.

item.title: Iraqi Kurds protest against Baghdad leader's moves to assert central control
item.description:
By Kawa Omar

DUHOK, Iraq, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Thousands of Kurds protested in their semi-autonomous region on Thursday against Iraqi Prime Minister Alial-Zaidi's campaign to take over oil fields controlled by Kurdish security forces and deploy federal troops at the region's international borders.

item.title: Co-leader of Germany's AfD criticises planned talks with Russian envoy
item.description:
By John O'Donnell

BERLIN, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel has criticised an AfD lawmaker's plans to meet a Kremlin envoy, dealing a blow to Moscow's efforts to woo the opposition far-right party as Russia tries to build support for resuming gas deliveries to Europe.

Bundestag member Markus Frohnmaier is preparing to attend talks in Abu Dhabi in February or March with Kirill Dmitriev, President Vladimir Putin's top business envoy, to discuss trade, including restarting gas supplies to Germany.

item.title: Iranian drone attack on Kuwait leaves two Italians dead
item.description: An Iranian drone attack killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait on Thursday, marking the first fatal Iranian attack on Kuwaiti territory since July.

item.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker capsizes off Ibiza, no pollution so far
item.description:
MADRID, Nov 26 (Reuters) - At least one crew member aboard a ship carrying diesel has died after the vessel capsized and partially sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza on Thursday, regional authorities said, adding there were no signs of pollution so far.

The Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre was sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona and may have been carrying up to 7,000 metric tons of diesel when it keeled over about 30 nautical miles (56 km) off Ibiza's northwestern coast, the Balearic Islands' interior department said.

item.title: Iran's supreme leader urges Guards-linked Basij volunteers to broaden social reach
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei called on Thursday on the Basij, nationwide volunteers affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards, to broaden their social reach and work towards making "every Iranian, a Basiji".

Since the start of the war launched by the United States and Israel in late February, Iranian authorities have relied on the Basij to help organise repeated pro-government rallies across the country, with state media portraying them as evidence of broad popular support for the Islamic Republic.

item.title: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi

CAIRO, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Hamas chief Khalil Al-Hayya said on Thursday the group was not prepared to withstand continued Israeli attacks, after local medics said Israeli strikes killed at least 10 people in Gaza, including the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education.

Hayya's statement was a rare sign of possible retaliation since Israel has stepped up attacks against the group in recent months, killing dozens of leaders and members.

item.title: Egypt prosecutors announce arrest of man over deadly truck disaster
item.description:
Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people.

The prosecution said the man had "admitted" to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, "causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course".

When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added.
